matches.title: AC Milan vs Atalanta
matches.description: Watch AC Milan vs Atalanta highlights and goals from Serie A on ReFooty: Football Highlights Hub. Match played on May 10, 2026. The lights of San Siro shone on a high-stakes Serie A encounter this Sunday, May 10, 2026, as two of Italy’s historic heavyweights faced off in a match defined by tactical precision and an unpredictable finale. Supporters witnessed a game where the momentum shifted dramatically between the two sides across ninety minutes of intense football. Atalanta's Clinical Start On the evening of May 10, 2026 , Atalanta arrived at the stadium with a clear plan to disrupt AC Milan . It took only seven minutes for the visitors to strike, as Ederson reacted quickest to a loose ball in the area to fire home with his right foot. The early lead forced the home side to chase, but Atalanta remained disciplined. In the 29th minute, the lead was doubled when Davide Zappacosta finished a move involving Charles De Ketelaere and Nikola Krstovic . While a VAR check briefly paused the celebrations, the goal was confirmed, leaving AC Milan with a mountain to climb before the break. Raspadori Extends the Lead The second half began much like the first ended, with Atalanta looking the more threatening side on the counter. In the 52nd minute, Giacomo Raspadori silenced the home crowd with a well-placed left-footed shot, assisted by Ederson following a clever ball from Marten de Roon . With a 3-0 cushion, the visitors appeared to be in total control. The AC Milan manager responded with a series of changes, bringing on Niclas Fuellkrug , Youssouf Fofana , and Pervis Estupiñán to inject some energy into a struggling side. A Frantic Finish at San Siro As the clock ticked toward the final whistle, the atmosphere grew increasingly tense. AC Milan finally found a lifeline in the 88th minute when Strahinja Pavlović rose highest to head home a cross from Samuele Ricci . The goal sparked a wave of cards for dissent, with Pervis Estupiñán , Adrien Rabiot , and Alexis Saelemaekers all entering the book as tempers flared. In the dying moments, Marten de Roon tripped Christopher Nkunku inside the box. After a tense VAR review, a penalty was awarded, which Nkunku coolly converted in the 94th minute. Despite the late pressure and a last-gasp header from Matteo Gabbia that went wide, Atalanta held on to secure the victory.

matches.title: Sassuolo vs AC Milan
matches.description: Watch Sassuolo vs AC Milan highlights and goals from Serie A on ReFooty: Football Highlights Hub. Match played on May 3, 2026. The MAPEI Stadium provided the backdrop for a high-stakes Serie A encounter as Sassuolo welcomed AC Milan on May 3, 2026. Both sides entered the pitch with plenty to prove in a match that would eventually be defined by clinical finishing and a critical moment of indiscipline that left the visitors shorthanded for the majority of the contest. Early Breakthrough and Tomori’s Dismissal The match ignited almost immediately, with the home side finding their rhythm within the opening minutes. In the 5th minute, a slick passing move involving M'Bala Nzola and Armand Laurienté carved open the AC Milan defense, allowing Domenico Berardi to strike with his clinical left foot. The goal sent the home crowd into raptures and forced the visitors into an early chase. As the AC Milan players attempted to regroup, their frustrations began to boil over, particularly for Fikayo Tomori , who was cautioned in the 9th minute for a heavy challenge. The complexion of the game changed irrevocably in the 24th minute. Fikayo Tomori , already on a yellow card, committed another mistimed challenge that left the referee with little choice but to brandish a second yellow followed by the red. Reduced to ten men with over an hour still to play, the sports narrative shifted toward a defensive damage-limitation exercise for the Rossoneri . Despite the numerical disadvantage, AC Milan tried to stay organized through the remainder of the first half , but Sassuolo dominated possession, expertly shifting the ball across the pitch to tire their opponents before the whistle. Laurienté Doubles the Advantage Any hopes of a second-half comeback for the visitors were dealt a heavy blow just moments after the restart. In the 47th minute, Kristian Thorstvedt turned provider, setting up Armand Laurienté to double the lead with a composed right-footed finish into the back of the net. With a 2-0 cushion, Sassuolo looked comfortable, while AC Milan manager responded with a flurry of tactical changes. Christian Pulisic , Santiago Gimenez , and Ruben Loftus-Cheek were all introduced in the 59th minute in a desperate attempt to inject some attacking impetus into the side, but the home defense remained resolute. Tensions Flare in the Closing Stages The final half-hour of the match was a stop-start affair characterized by a flurry of bookings as tensions flared. Samuele Ricci and Ruben Loftus-Cheek were both cautioned for the visitors—the latter for simulation—while Sassuolo ’s Ulisses Garcia and Cristian Volpato also saw yellow. Each chance for a Milan revival was met by a disciplined home side that refused to relinquish their 57% share of the ball. In the dying moments, the drama continued as Alieu Fadera was booked for diving, highlighting the desperate nature of the closing exchanges. Despite late pressure from the visitors, including crosses from Pervis Estupinan and Zachary Athekame , Stefano Turati and the Sassuolo backline held firm. When the final whistle blew after four minutes of stoppage time, it confirmed a professional performance from the hosts, who capitalized perfectly on their man advantage to secure all three points.

matches.title: AC Milan vs Juventus
matches.description: Watch AC Milan vs Juventus highlights and goals from Serie A on ReFooty: Football Highlights Hub. Match played on April 26, 2026. On a night where fine margins defined the outcome, AC Milan and Juventus battled to a frantic stalemate that was ultimately decided by the intervention of technology. The San Siro bore witness to a high-stakes tactical chess match on April 26, 2026, where a disallowed first-half strike served as the afternoon’s painful peak for the visitors. First Half: VAR Denies the Breakthrough The match began with both sides searching for rhythm, though the early exchanges were defined more by defensive discipline than offensive flair. Juventus looked to exert control through Jeremie Boga’s set-piece delivery, but his 11th-minute corner failed to find a teammate. The intensity boiled over in the 20th minute when Andrea Cambiaso earned the game’s first yellow card, setting a physical tone for the afternoon. The defining moment of the first half arrived in the 37th minute. Juventus believed they had snatched the lead when Khephren Thuram-Ulien found the back of the net, sparking wild celebrations in the away end. However, the joy was short-lived. Following a lengthy VAR review, the referee revoked the goal , ruling Thuram-Ulien offside by the narrowest of margins. The tension remained high as Milan’s Davide Bartesaghi was booked just a minute later, ensuring the sides went into the tunnel level. Second Half: Tactical Shuffles and Defensive Grit Returning for the second half , Milan manager opted for an immediate change, replacing the cautioned Bartesaghi with Pervis Estupinan. The home side struggled to test the Juventus keeper, with Christian Pulisic being withdrawn after an hour for the physical presence of Niclas Fuellkrug. As the clock ticked down, the sports spectacle became a battle of attrition. Juventus introduced Teun Koopmeiners and Emil Holm to inject fresh energy, while Milan turned to Christopher Nkunku in place of Rafael Leao. Despite the changes, clear-cut openings remained a rarity. Jeremie Boga and Estupinan both saw yellow as the play became increasingly fragmented by tactical fouls. Late Drama and Final Whistle The final ten minutes offered the most significant chance for a winner. In the 86th minute, Emil Holm delivered a pinpoint cross into the box, finding the head of Jonathan David. The striker, however, could only watch in frustration as his effort drifted agonizingly wide of the post. Shortly after, Manuel Locatelli was lucky to stay on the pitch after a reckless challenge on Adrien Rabiot resulted in a yellow card. In the dying embers of stoppage time, Juventus thought they had one final opening, but Dusan Vlahovic was caught in the offside trap in the 93rd minute. As the referee blew the final whistle at 90+7', the stats reflected the parity of the match , with Juventus edging possession at 52% to Milan’s 48%. For both giants, it was a night of what-might-have-been in the race for the Scudetto. Final Score: AC Milan 0-0 Juventus

matches.title: AC Milan vs Cagliari

The lights of the legendary San Siro stadium shone brightly on 2026-05-24 for a clash that promised tactical intrigue and high-stakes drama. Fans gathered to witness a fixture where every transition mattered and momentum shifted with every whistle. Early Fireworks at the San Siro The match exploded into life almost immediately. In just the second minute, AC Milan took the lead through Alexis Saelemaekers , who finished clinically with his right foot. The move was orchestrated by a key pass from Fikayo Tomori , which found Santiago Gimenez , who provided the decisive assist. In the chaos of the early goal, Cagliari 's Ze Pedro was cautioned with a yellow card as the visitors struggled to find their footing. A Resilient Response Despite the early setback, the visitors began to find their rhythm. In the 20th minute, Cagliari found their equalizer. After a corner from Adam Obert led to a blocked effort by Yerry Mina , the ball fell to Gennaro Borrelli , who made no mistake with a left-footed strike to level the score. AC Milan attempted to regain control, with Youssouf Fofana seeing a header comfortably saved by Elia Caprile just after the half-hour mark, but the teams went into the interval on level terms. Momentum Shifts and Second Half Drama The second half saw AC Milan introduce Christian Pulisic to add more attacking threat. However, it was Cagliari who seized the initiative. In the 57th minute, Juan Rodriguez pounced on a loose ball to head home, putting the visitors in front. The goal sparked frustration in the Milan ranks, with Strahinja Pavlovic receiving a booking and goalkeeper Mike Maignan also seeing yellow for dissent as the home side protested the unfolding events. Desperate Final Efforts In a bid to rescue a point, AC Milan made a flurry of substitutions, bringing on Luka Modric , Rafael Leao , and Niclas Fuellkrug . Despite intense pressure and several corner kicks delivered by Modric , the equalizer remained elusive. Cagliari 's defense, led by Alberto Dossena , remained resolute, intercepting crucial crosses deep into stoppage time. Even as Ibrahim Sulemana received a late yellow card for a tactical foul, the visitors held their nerve until the final whistle to secure a memorable victory.

matches.title: Genoa vs AC Milan
matches.description: Watch Genoa vs AC Milan highlights and goals from Serie A on ReFooty: Football Highlights Hub. Match played on May 17, 2026. The Stadio Luigi Ferraris set the stage for a compelling Serie A encounter between Genoa and AC Milan on May 17, 2026. Both sides entered the pitch knowing that tactical discipline and clinical finishing would be the deciding factors in a match of high stakes. Tactical Stalemate in the Opening Period The first half was characterized by a cagey tactical battle where clear-cut opportunities were hard to come by. Santiago Gimenez provided a rare moment of individual flair in the 30th minute with an audacious bicycle kick that drifted wide of the target. As the halftime whistle approached, AC Milan ramped up the pressure, and Youssouf Fofana saw his goalbound header comfortably gathered by Justin Bijlow . Despite the territorial battle, both teams headed into the tunnels with the scoreline still level. Second-Half Breakthrough The game exploded into life shortly after the restart. In the 48th minute, a lapse in judgment from Genoa goalkeeper Justin Bijlow resulted in a penalty after he tripped Christopher Nkunku . The French forward stepped up to the spot and calmly converted with his right foot in the 50th minute, sending the keeper the wrong way. The opening goal sparked a more aggressive approach from both sides, leading to a flurry of yellow cards, including one for Vitinha for dissent as the intensity of the match heightened. Late Drama and Nerve-Wracking Finish As the match entered its final phase, AC Milan seemed to have secured the points in the 81st minute. Christian Pulisic turned provider, setting up Zachary Athekame , who unleashed a powerful strike from outside the box to make it 2-0. However, Genoa found a lifeline in the 87th minute when Johan Vasquez pounced on a defensive blunder by Koni De Winter to pull one back. The closing minutes were frantic; Niclas Fuellkrug missed a golden opportunity to restore the two-goal lead, and Bijlow made a stunning save to deny Pulisic in stoppage time. Ultimately, despite Genoa controlling 62% of the possession, AC Milan held firm to clinch a hard-fought victory.
